The existing read picks the newest non-NULL row; this one must return the row for the month asked for, and report 'no row' distinctly from 'row with NULL capacity'. Honour RD4: the caller stores 0, so the port must let the caller tell the two cases apart. Tier 1 of 4 of roadmap RM67-vehicle-monthly-metrics-table (Linear MAG-73); it exists because tier 2 in analytics cannot copy the capacity without it.

review.brief: Review the diff of commits e6edbac and dbfd6cf on ft/RM67-MAG-73-vehicle-monthly-metrics-table. Check: (1) module-boundary compliance - nothing outside internal/charging except the KB guide, no other module touched; (2) every doc-pack convention, especially ai/go-conventions.md on units, time zone and no pgtype in public types or tests; (3) the integration tests assert design.md's Test Contract T1-T7 and T4b values, NOT whatever the implementation does; (4) the three-state contract (no row / row with NULL capacity / row with capacity) is real in both the code and the tests; (5) the month is normalized in SQL, never in Go - no hand-rolled UTC-midnight construction (tz-guard); (6) no migration, no new index, and LatestMeasuredCapacity / packCapacityKWh are untouched; (7) the tasks.md 'Not in this change' list was respected; (8) read-heavy Performance-Profile compliance; (9) anti-gaming - no task title, criterion or Test Contract expectation was weakened; (10) docs-track-structural-change: internal/charging/AGENTS.md and kkpa/context/workflows/vehicle-monthly-metrics.md are correct and not stale. Signals: go build, go vet, gofmt -l and make lint were assistant-run and clean (0 issues). The suite was run and reported passing by the OWNER, not by the assistant - judge test quality by reading the tests, never by running them.

findings.note: internal/charging/db/query.sql.go:203-213 — the generated doc comment on EffectiveCapacityForPeriod still reads '...own read (RM67 tier 1)...' and '...for a thin month (RD4)...'. The current source comment in internal/charging/db/query.sql (same query) no longer has these two citations — decision D-L6 says the leader stripped them from three comments. sqlc copies the SQL comment into the Go doc comment verbatim (confirmed against the pre-existing LatestMeasuredCapacity query, whose comment matches word for word in both files), so this mismatch means query.sql.go was not regenerated after the query.sql edit. Two problems: (a) the checked-in generated file no longer matches what `make sqlc` produces from the current source, breaking codegen reproducibility; (b) the stale comment still carries a roadmap tier and a decision ID, which the B2 comment rule forbids. Fix: re-run `make sqlc` so query.sql.go regenerates from the cleaned-up query.sql comment.
